clues.label: A musical characteristic
clues.text: The music largely sidesteps functional harmony, moving instead through whole-tone and modal collections and parallel chords that earlier counterpoint would have forbidden outright.

clues.label: A historical event connected to the composer
clues.text: At the Universal Exposition of 1889 the composer heard a Javanese gamelan ensemble for the first time, an encounter he was still referring to years afterwards.

clues.label: A biographical detail
clues.text: The composer trained at his country's national Conservatoire and won the Prix de Rome, though he disliked his residency in Italy and cut it short.

clues.label: An anecdote
clues.text: In this set the title of each piece is printed at the end rather than the top, so the player meets the music before its name.

explanation.summary: French Conservatoire training, the 1889 gamelan encounter, and non-functional harmony point to Claude Debussy, working in Paris in 1910.

points.text: Whole-tone writing and planing parallel chords are the harmonic signature of Debussy.
The Exposition was the Paris one of 1889, held for the centenary of the Revolution; the gamelan left its mark on his later textures.
The national Conservatoire is the Paris Conservatoire, and the Prix de Rome places him inside the French institutional tradition.
Titles printed at the end of each piece is a distinctive feature of the Préludes.
